source_meta.issue links: Relates:outward:MC-186647:Villager price changes are extremely inconsistent, and completely break in combination with hero of the village | Duplicate:inward:MC-230794:Villager Trading Gives More Loot Than Taken | Relates:inward:MC-268017:Re-curing fully discounted villagers resets/doesn't change discounts on that villager
source_meta._title: The discount for curing a villager is multiplied if the villager is reinfected and cured again

stor.environment: Vanilla Minecraft Java Edition 1.20 in a fresh single-player world, using Creative mode, Hard difficulty, and cheats enabled. Use one player for every trade and both curing cycles. Default controls are assumed: E for inventory, T for chat, right-click for Use Item/Place Block, and Esc to close a screen.
preconditions: Use Minecraft Java Edition 1.20 because it is the latest stable release explicitly listed under the report's affected versions.
Do not use 23w31a for this reproduction; the report lists that snapshot as its fix version.
Use the same player for the initial trade, both golden-apple interactions, and all price inspections so that the test follows one player's curing-related discount.

No seed, coordinates, server configuration, game mode, villager profession, or specific trade is supplied by the report. The fresh Creative single-player world, farmer profession, and containment chamber are practical choices for deterministic execution.

Choose an isolated test location with no other villagers, zombies, composters, or other job-site blocks nearby. Do not obtain Hero of the Village or perform unrelated actions that change villager reputation during the procedure.

Hard difficulty is used because a villager killed by a zombie has a 100% conversion chance on Hard, avoiding the 50% conversion chance on Normal and death without conversion on Easy. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ACuring_a_zombie_villager?utm_source=openai))

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the unmodified Java Edition 1.20 release installation and launch the game.
steps.success_cue: The main menu identifies the running version as Minecraft Java Edition 1.20.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, create a new world in Creative mode with Allow Cheats enabled, and enter the world. The seed may remain random because the report supplies no required seed or coordinates.
steps.success_cue: The player is in a newly loaded world, can fly, and has access to the Creative inventory.

steps.action: Move or fly to a reasonably flat location away from any visible village, villagers, zombies, composters, or other job-site blocks.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space to start flying; use W to move
steps.success_cue: An isolated, level construction area is available and no other villagers or zombies are visible nearby.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat, enter the difficulty command exactly as shown including the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the difficulty has been set to Hard.

steps.action: Open chat, disable natural mob spawning so that the only regular zombies near the test are the ones deliberately spawned, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the doMobSpawning game rule is now false.

steps.action: Open chat, set the world to daytime, and press Enter. Daytime helps the unemployed villager claim the composter while the later roof protects spawned zombies from sunlight.
steps.success_cue: The world is visibly in daytime and the command succeeds.

steps.action: Build a containment chamber from opaque solid blocks: make a 5-by-5-block floor, construct walls two blocks high around its perimeter to leave a 3-by-3-block interior, and cover the entire chamber with a solid roof above the interior. In the center of one wall, leave out only the upper wall block while keeping the lower wall block in place. This one-block-high interaction window must let the player see and use items on entities without allowing adult villagers or zombies to walk out.
steps.exact_input: Right-click to place blocks; left-click to remove an incorrectly placed block
steps.success_cue: The chamber has a fully covered 3-by-3 interior, two-block-high walls, and one upper-level interaction window with a solid lower block beneath it.

steps.action: Press E to open the Creative inventory. Use the Search Items tab to obtain and place on the hotbar: one Composter, one Villager Spawn Egg, one Zombie Spawn Egg, at least two Splash Potions of Weakness, at least two regular Golden Apples, and spare solid blocks. Use the non-enchanted Golden Apple, not the Enchanted Golden Apple.
steps.success_cue: The required job-site block, spawn eggs, curing items, and spare blocks are available in the hotbar or inventory.

steps.action: Select the Composter and place it on an interior floor block in a corner of the chamber, where it will remain reachable by the villager.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one composter is present inside the chamber and no other job-site block is nearby.

steps.action: Select the Villager Spawn Egg, aim through the interaction window at an empty interior floor block, and use the egg exactly once.
steps.success_cue: One adult villager is inside the chamber and cannot leave.

steps.action: Wait without placing another job-site block until the villager claims the composter and changes into a farmer. If necessary, remain nearby while daytime continues.
steps.success_cue: The villager wears the farmer's straw hat, and opening its interface identifies it as a Novice Farmer.

steps.action: Aim at the farmer through the interaction window and use the villager to open its trading screen. Identify a novice offer in which the farmer buys wheat, carrots, potatoes, or beetroots and gives one emerald. Note the crop type and the offer's row or position, then close the screen without trading yet. Farmers buy crops, making this a convenient high-input offer for comparing the same trade through both curing cycles. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AVillager_trading_hall?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: One specific crop-for-emerald offer has been selected for the entire test, and its crop type and position are recorded.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory, search for the exact crop requested by the selected offer, and put at least one full stack of that crop in the player inventory.
steps.success_cue: The inventory contains at least the quantity required to execute the selected farmer offer once.

steps.action: Open the farmer's trading screen again. Place the requested crop quantity into the trade input slot and take the emerald from the output slot to complete the offer exactly once. Do not repeat the trade. Completing one trade locks the villager's profession and offers. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3AVillager_trading_hall?utm_source=openai))
steps.exact_input: Right-click; left-click the required crop into the input slot; left-click the emerald output
steps.success_cue: One trade completes, the player receives an emerald, and the villager retains the farmer profession and selected offer.

steps.action: Open the trading screen once more, select the same crop-for-emerald offer, and record its currently displayed crop input count as the locked pre-cure baseline. Do not execute another trade; close the screen with Esc.
steps.success_cue: The exact offer and its locked pre-cure input count have been recorded, and the trading screen is closed.

steps.action: Select the Zombie Spawn Egg, aim through the interaction window at an empty interior block close to the farmer, and use the egg exactly once.
steps.success_cue: One regular zombie and the same farmer villager are both alive inside the roofed chamber.

steps.action: Remain near the chamber and wait for the regular zombie to attack the villager until the villager transforms into a zombie villager. Do not attack either entity. On Hard difficulty, a villager killed by a zombie converts instead of being lost. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ACuring_a_zombie_villager?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The farmer has become a zombie villager, while the separate regular zombie is still present inside the chamber.

steps.action: While standing within 10 blocks of the chamber, open chat and execute the command exactly as shown to remove regular zombies without targeting the differently typed zombie villager.
steps.success_cue: The regular zombie disappears, and the zombie villager remains alone and alive inside the chamber.

steps.action: Select a Splash Potion of Weakness, aim through the interaction window so the potion directly splashes the zombie villager, and throw it using the Use Item control.
steps.success_cue: Gray status-effect particles appear around the zombie villager, indicating that Weakness is active. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ACuring_a_zombie_villager?utm_source=openai))

steps.action: Immediately select a regular Golden Apple, aim directly at the weakened zombie villager through the interaction window, and use the apple on the entity. Do not eat the apple or throw it on the floor.
steps.success_cue: The zombie villager begins shaking and emits curing particles, confirming that the first curing process has started. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ACuring_a_zombie_villager?utm_source=openai))

steps.action: Stay close enough to keep the chamber loaded and wait until the first curing process finishes. Do not spawn another zombie, damage the zombie villager, leave the world, or move far enough away to unload the area. Conversion normally takes approximately three to five minutes. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ACuring_a_zombie_villager?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The shaking zombie villager has converted back into a normal adult farmer villager, and no regular zombie is present.

steps.action: Use the cured farmer to open the trading screen, select the same locked crop-for-emerald offer recorded earlier, and record its displayed crop input count as the first-cure value. Do not execute the trade. Close the screen with Esc.
steps.success_cue: The first-cure input count for the exact same locked offer has been recorded, and the trading screen is closed.

steps.action: Select the Zombie Spawn Egg again and use it exactly once on an empty interior block close to the cured farmer.
steps.success_cue: One new regular zombie is inside the chamber with the same once-cured farmer.

steps.action: Wait for the new zombie to attack and reinfect the same farmer. Do not attack either entity or introduce another villager. Hard difficulty makes the conversion deterministic. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ACuring_a_zombie_villager?utm_source=openai))
steps.success_cue: The once-cured farmer has become a zombie villager again, and the regular zombie remains present.

steps.action: While within 10 blocks of the chamber, open chat and execute the same regular-zombie removal command.
steps.success_cue: The regular zombie disappears, leaving only the reinfected zombie villager inside the chamber.

steps.action: Select the second Splash Potion of Weakness and throw it through the interaction window so that it directly splashes the reinfected zombie villager.
steps.success_cue: Gray status-effect particles appear around the reinfected zombie villager, confirming Weakness is active. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ACuring_a_zombie_villager?utm_source=openai))

steps.action: Immediately select the second regular Golden Apple and use it directly on the weakened zombie villager through the interaction window.
steps.success_cue: The reinfected zombie villager begins shaking and emits curing particles, confirming that the second curing process has started. ([minecraft.wiki](https://minecraft.wiki/w/Tutorial%3ACuring_a_zombie_villager?utm_source=openai))

steps.action: Remain near the loaded chamber and wait until the second curing process finishes. Do not perform any unrelated villager interactions during the wait.
steps.success_cue: The shaking zombie villager has converted back into the same adult farmer for the second time, and no regular zombie is present.

steps.action: Immediately use the twice-cured farmer to open its trading screen. Select the exact same locked crop-for-emerald offer used for the pre-cure and first-cure recordings, and leave the trading screen open without executing the offer.
steps.success_cue: The twice-cured farmer's trading screen is open with the previously recorded crop-for-emerald offer selected and its current input count visible.

stor.handoff_condition: The same villager has completed two player-performed curing cycles, and its trading screen is now open on the same locked crop-for-emerald offer used for the pre-cure and first-cure recordings. Hand control to the observation subsystem while the current input count remains visible.
uncertainties: The report contains no formal Steps to Reproduce section. The procedure is reconstructed from the description's required order: cure a villager, reinfect that same villager, cure it again, and inspect its trade discount.
The report does not specify a single preferred affected version. Java Edition 1.20 is selected because it is the latest stable release listed as affected and avoids snapshot-specific setup.

The report does not specify game mode, world type, seed, coordinates, villager profession, or trade. Creative mode, an isolated chamber, and a novice farmer crop-purchase offer are practical implementation choices rather than report requirements.
A farmer's exact crop offer and starting input count can vary. The executor must record and revisit the identical locked offer rather than assuming a particular crop or numerical price.
The report does not specify whether a baseline price was recorded. Pre-cure and first-cure recordings are added so the observation subsystem has unambiguous comparison points after the second cure.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-200492:Paths generated over shallow water do not replace the water with planks
source_meta._title: Villages replace ice with path blocks instead of wood

stor.environment: Single-player Minecraft Java Edition 1.16.2 world created directly in that version, using the Default world type, seed -7882263134696652088, Generate Structures enabled, Creative mode, and commands/cheats enabled.
preconditions: Install and launch the unmodified Minecraft Java Edition release 1.16.2; do not use 1.18 Pre-release 5 or a later version because the report lists 1.18 Pre-release 5 as the fix version.
Create a new world directly in 1.16.2. Do not reuse a world whose target chunks were previously generated in another Minecraft version.
Use the exact report seed: -7882263134696652088.
Keep Generate Structures enabled so the village can generate.
Enable commands by selecting Creative mode and ensuring Allow Cheats is ON; the supplied teleport command requires command permission.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the historical installation for Minecraft Java Edition release 1.16.2, and launch the game.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft main menu is open and displays version 1.16.2.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, then select Create New World to begin configuring a fresh world.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Set Game Mode to Creative. Ensure Allow Cheats is set to ON so the report's teleport command can be executed.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Cheats: ON
steps.success_cue: The world-creation screen shows Creative mode and Allow Cheats: ON.

steps.action: Select More World Options and enter the report's seed into the seed field. Preserve the leading minus sign and every digit.
steps.success_cue: The seed field contains exactly -7882263134696652088.

steps.action: On the same options screen, leave World Type set to Default and verify that Generate Structures is ON.
steps.exact_input: World Type: Default; Generate Structures: ON
steps.success_cue: The options show the Default world type with structure generation enabled.

steps.action: Select Done if necessary to return to the main world-creation screen, then select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: Minecraft begins generating and loading the new world.

steps.action: Wait at the initial spawn point until the loading screen has closed, nearby terrain is rendered, and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the Overworld and the initial terrain has finished loading sufficiently for chat and movement to respond.

steps.action: Press T, or the currently bound Open Chat control, to open in-game chat.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to accept a command.

steps.action: Enter the report's teleport command exactly as written, including the leading slash, dimension, coordinates, yaw, and pitch. Press Enter once to execute it.
steps.success_cue: The player is teleported a very large distance to the report location in the Overworld, with the command-provided viewing rotation applied.

steps.action: Do not move, rotate, place, or break blocks after teleporting. Wait until the destination chunks and village terrain have rendered, the loading pause has ended, and controls respond normally.
steps.success_cue: The destination terrain is fully visible, no loading screen is present, and the game responds normally while the player remains at the teleported position.

steps.action: Press F3 to open the debug overlay and verify that the player is in the Overworld near X -135.95, Y 63.00, Z -303308.65. Then press F3 again to close the overlay without moving or changing the camera direction.
steps.success_cue: The reported destination coordinates and Overworld dimension have been verified, and the unobstructed game view is restored.

steps.action: Leave the player at the command-set position and viewing rotation. Confirm that the generated village area and the nearby frozen water or ice terrain associated with its path are loaded in the view; do not modify any blocks before handing control to the observation subsystem.
steps.success_cue: The target village terrain, including the path area adjacent to or crossing the frozen water body, is loaded and available for visual inspection in its untouched generated state.

stor.handoff_condition: The teleport has generated or loaded the target village chunks in Minecraft Java Edition 1.16.2. The player remains near X -135.95, Y 63.00, Z -303308.65 with yaw -178.50 and pitch 22.50, and the untouched village path and frozen-water area are fully rendered. Begin observation of the generated blocks.
uncertainties: The report does not state a game mode. Creative mode with cheats is used as a practical execution choice because the supplied teleport command requires permission and Creative mode avoids unrelated survival hazards.

The report does not name a specific village building, path segment, or individual block coordinate. The supplied player coordinates and camera rotation are therefore preserved exactly and treated as the intended inspection viewpoint.
The attached screenshots are referenced by the report but their visual contents were not supplied, so they cannot be used to further distinguish the precise path segment.
The report lists several affected versions. Release 1.16.2 is recommended because it is explicitly listed as affected and was independently confirmed in the supplied Mojira comments.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-248331:The "minecraft:woodland_mansion/1x2_a2" structure generates with one dehydrated farmland block
source_meta._title: One farmland block in plains_large_farm_1 has moisture level 0

stor.environment: A new single-player Creative-mode Superflat world in Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.2, with commands enabled. A Superflat world and disabled random block ticks are practical choices that make the placed template easy to access and preserve its initial farmland states; they are not stated requirements of the report.
preconditions: Launch the exact Java Edition version 1.19.2. This is an affected release in which the report explicitly confirms the supplied /place command reproduction.
Use a disposable test world rather than an important existing world.
The player must have permission to execute commands. In single-player, create the world in Creative mode with Allow Cheats enabled.
No particular world seed, biome, naturally generated village, datapack, resource pack, or dedicated server is required by the report.
Use the exact structure template identifier minecraft:village/plains/houses/plains_large_farm_1.

Perform the placement only after setting randomTickSpeed to 0 if preserving the template's initial block states for inspection is desired. This is a practical determinism measure, not a requirement stated by the report.

steps.action: Start the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for Minecraft Java Edition 1.19.2, and launch the game. Do not use 1.19.3 or a later version for this reproduction.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen is open and displays version 1.19.2.

steps.action: From the title screen, open Singleplayer and select Create New World.
steps.success_cue: The Create New World configuration screen is open.

steps.action: Configure the test world for Creative mode and ensure commands are permitted. Open More World Options and change World Type to Superflat so the structure can be placed in an unobstructed area. No specific seed is needed.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Cheats: ON; World Type: Superflat
steps.success_cue: The new world is configured as Creative, commands are allowed, and the selected world type is Superflat.

steps.action: Select Create New World and wait for world generation and chunk loading to finish. Do not continue while the loading screen is visible.
steps.success_cue: The player is in the world, nearby flat terrain is rendered, and movement responds normally.

steps.action: Remain on level, unobstructed ground. If the spawn location contains an obstruction, use the movement controls to move to a clear section of the Superflat terrain before placing the template.
steps.exact_input: Default movement controls: W, A, S, and D
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a clear area with enough unobstructed terrain for a large farm template to appear.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat. Enter the command that disables random block ticks, including the leading slash, and press Enter. This preserves the block states initially placed by the structure template while the observation subsystem examines them.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a red syntax or permission error, and randomTickSpeed is set to 0.

steps.action: Wait until chat has closed and the game view responds normally. Keep the player in the same clear placement area.
steps.success_cue: The normal game view is visible, the player remains in the clear area, and controls are responsive.

steps.action: Press T to open in-game chat for the structure placement command.
steps.success_cue: The chat input field is open and ready to receive a command.

steps.action: Type the report's structure placement command exactly as supplied, including the leading slash. Do not alter the structure identifier, add coordinates, or substitute another village farm template.
steps.success_cue: The complete command is visible in the chat input field exactly as specified and has not yet been submitted.

steps.action: Press Enter once to execute the structure placement command.
steps.success_cue: The command is accepted without a red syntax or permission error, and the plains large farm template is placed at the command's placement position.

steps.action: Wait until all blocks of the placed structure have rendered and player movement responds normally. Do not repeatedly execute the placement command.
steps.success_cue: A single plains large farm structure containing farmland, crops, water, and its associated farm layout is fully visible and the game is responsive.

steps.action: If the structure obstructs the player's view, use Creative flight to move above or beside it without breaking, placing, trampling, or otherwise updating any farm blocks. With default controls, double-tap Space to begin flying, hold Space to rise, and use W, A, S, or D to obtain an unobstructed view.
steps.exact_input: Double-tap Space; then Space and W/A/S/D as needed
steps.success_cue: The player has an unobstructed view of the placed farm, no farm blocks have been deliberately interacted with, and randomTickSpeed remains 0.

stor.handoff_condition: The command has placed exactly one minecraft:village/plains/houses/plains_large_farm_1 template, the entire farm has rendered, random block ticks remain disabled, and the player is positioned to inspect the farm without having modified its blocks. Hand control to the observation subsystem for block-state inspection.
uncertainties: The report does not identify the affected farmland block's coordinates or relative position within the template. The observation subsystem will need to inspect the farmland blocks in the placed structure.

The report explicitly confirms the supplied /place reproduction in 1.19 and 1.19.2 but does not supply an equivalent deterministic placement procedure for the affected 1.16.x versions; therefore, 1.19.2 is recommended.
Creative mode, a Superflat world, and randomTickSpeed 0 are practical execution choices rather than requirements asserted by the report.
The report does not specify a seed, biome, player coordinates, viewing direction, or required placement orientation.

source_meta.issue links: Relates:inward:MC-227469:Leatherworker villagers use the lava cauldron or powder snow cauldron produces water sounds | Relates:inward:MCPE-43961:Villagers lose their job site association with cauldrons filled with lava
source_meta._title: Cauldrons filled with water, lava or powder snow cannot be used as a workstation for villagers

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft Java Edition snapshot 21w11a. Use this as the primary reproduction version because it is the latest version listed in the report's affected-version range. Do not substitute 21w13a or a later version.
stor.environment: Single-player Java Edition world in Creative mode with cheats enabled, preferably a newly generated Superflat world with structures disabled. Run the reproduction independently three times: once with a Water Bucket, once with a Lava Bucket, and once with a Powder Snow Bucket. Use a fresh world for each variant to prevent prior villager job-site state from affecting the next run.
preconditions: Install and launch the exact Java Edition snapshot 21w11a from the Minecraft Launcher.
Use an unmodified client without mods or non-default datapacks that change villagers, professions, cauldrons, schedules, or block interactions.
Create a separate fresh world for each filling-material variant: water, lava, and powder snow.
Set Game Mode to Creative and enable cheats so the required blocks, items, spawn egg, and time commands are available.
Prefer the Superflat world type and disable structure generation so no village or unrelated workstation blocks are near the test location.
The test villager must be an adult unemployed villager, not a baby, nitwit, or already employed villager.
Do not place any other villager workstation blocks in the test world.
Do not trade with the villager. Trading can lock its profession and alter the job-site test condition.
Perform the trigger only after the villager has visibly become a leatherworker and the leatherworker trade interface has been used to confirm the profession.

steps.action: In the Minecraft Launcher, select the installation for Java Edition snapshot 21w11a and start the game. Confirm the version displayed on the title screen before continuing.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft title screen identifies the running version as 21w11a.

steps.action: Select Singleplayer, choose Create New World, and configure a fresh Creative-mode test world. Enable cheats. For a controlled environment, select the Superflat world type and turn Generate Structures off. Create the world.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Cheats: ON; World Type: Superflat; Generate Structures: OFF
steps.success_cue: The player has spawned in a new, flat world and can fly and instantly break blocks.

steps.action: Wait before setting up the test until the nearby terrain has rendered and movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The ground around the player is visible, no chunk-loading screen is present, and normal movement and inventory controls respond immediately.

steps.action: Set the world to daytime so the villager can enter its normal job-site acquisition period. Press T to open chat, type the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: The world changes to daytime and the command reports successful time adjustment.

steps.action: Keep the test at daytime. Press T, enter the gamerule command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Chat confirms that the doDaylightCycle gamerule is now false and the sun no longer advances.

steps.action: Open the Creative inventory with E. Obtain one Cauldron and place it in an accessible hotbar slot. The hotbar is the row of nine item slots along the bottom of the screen.
steps.success_cue: A Cauldron item is visible in one of the nine hotbar slots.

steps.action: While the Creative inventory is open, obtain one Villager Spawn Egg and place it in another hotbar slot.
steps.success_cue: A Villager Spawn Egg is visible in the hotbar.

steps.action: Obtain the bucket required for the current independent variant and place it in the hotbar. Use a Water Bucket for the first run, a Lava Bucket in a fresh second run, and a Powder Snow Bucket in a fresh third run.
steps.exact_input: Run 1: Water Bucket; Run 2: Lava Bucket; Run 3: Powder Snow Bucket
steps.success_cue: Exactly one of the specified filled buckets for the current run is available in the hotbar.

steps.action: Close the inventory with E. Move to an open, level location where no other workstation blocks or villagers are visible nearby.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing in a clear test area with no village structures, villagers, or other workstation blocks nearby.

steps.action: Select the Cauldron in the hotbar, aim at the top surface of a ground block, and use the place-block control, which is right-click by default, once.
steps.success_cue: One empty cauldron is standing upright on the ground with open space beside it.

steps.action: Select the Villager Spawn Egg in the hotbar. Aim at the ground directly beside the empty cauldron and right-click once to spawn a villager.
steps.exact_input: Right-click once while holding Villager Spawn Egg
steps.success_cue: One villager is present beside the empty cauldron.

steps.action: Inspect the spawned villager before proceeding. It must be an adult unemployed villager. If it is a baby, wears the green nitwit robe, or already displays an unrelated profession outfit, remove it without changing the cauldron and spawn a replacement beside the cauldron. Repeat until a suitable adult unemployed villager is present.
steps.success_cue: A single adult villager that is neither a nitwit nor visibly assigned to another profession is beside the empty cauldron.

steps.action: Do not fill the cauldron yet. Wait while the villager can reach or stand near the empty cauldron. Continue only after it adopts the leatherworker profession; profession acquisition may be accompanied by green particles and a change to the leatherworker outfit.
steps.success_cue: The villager has changed from unemployed to the leatherworker profession while the cauldron is still empty.

steps.action: Confirm the profession without completing a trade. With an empty hand or any non-interacting item selected, aim at the villager and right-click once to open its trading interface. Verify that the interface identifies it as a novice leatherworker, then close the interface with Esc. Do not place an item into a trade slot and do not take any trade output.
steps.exact_input: Right-click villager; verify Leatherworker/Novice; press Esc
steps.success_cue: The trade interface has confirmed that the villager is a leatherworker, no trade has been completed, and the normal world view is open again.

steps.action: Select the filled bucket assigned to the current run in the hotbar. Verify visually that the cauldron is still empty before using the bucket.
steps.exact_input: Water Bucket, Lava Bucket, or Powder Snow Bucket for the current run
steps.success_cue: The chosen filled bucket is held in the player's active hand, the confirmed leatherworker remains near the test site, and the cauldron is still empty.

steps.action: Aim directly at the inside or upper rim of the empty cauldron and use the bucket once with the use-item control, which is right-click by default. Do not interact with the villager or cauldron again after this click.
steps.exact_input: Right-click the empty cauldron once with the selected Water Bucket, Lava Bucket, or Powder Snow Bucket
steps.success_cue: The same cauldron that served as the confirmed leatherworker workstation now visibly contains the selected water, lava, or powder snow material.

stor.handoff_condition: The selected bucket has just been used once on the previously empty cauldron after that cauldron was confirmed as the villager's leatherworker job site. The cauldron visibly contains the selected material. Stop all player input and begin observation immediately. Repeat the complete plan in separate fresh worlds for the other two bucket variants.
uncertainties: The report does not specify a world seed, world type, game mode, enclosure, or exact time of day. A fresh Creative Superflat world with structures disabled and frozen daytime is a practical deterministic setup rather than a stated report requirement.

The original reproduction bullets explicitly say to add water or lava. Powder snow is added by the issue title, affected-version information, and the later report comment stating that powder snow cauldrons are additionally affected.

The report does not state a fixed delay for villager profession acquisition. The plan therefore uses the visible leatherworker profession and its trade-interface label as the readiness condition instead of relying on an arbitrary waiting period.

The three filling materials are treated as independent variants. A fresh world per material is recommended to avoid profession locking, stale job-site memory, or block state left by a previous variant.

stor.recommended_version: Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1 Snapshot 3 for the trigger phase; prepare the same world and its claimed bed in 26.1 Snapshot 2, the immediately preceding snapshot.
stor.environment: Single-player Minecraft: Java Edition using the integrated server. Use the official Minecraft Launcher with installations for 26.1 Snapshot 2 and 26.1 Snapshot 3. Use Creative mode, commands enabled, Peaceful difficulty, a Superflat Overworld with structures disabled, and no mods or datapacks. Both installations must use the same game directory, or the exact same world save must be copied from the Snapshot 2 saves directory to the Snapshot 3 saves directory.
preconditions: Install or create launcher installations for both Minecraft: Java Edition 26.1 Snapshot 2 and 26.1 Snapshot 3. Snapshot 3 is the affected version; do not use Snapshot 4 or a later version for the trigger phase.

The original report's later clarification states that the bed must already exist before the world is opened in 26.1 Snapshot 3. This plan uses 26.1 Snapshot 2 as the deterministic source version because it immediately precedes Snapshot 3.
Ensure both launcher installations can access the same world save. If custom game directories are used, copy the complete source-world folder rather than creating a new world in Snapshot 3.
Back up the source world before opening it in Snapshot 3. Snapshot testing can damage or permanently convert worlds.
Use a fresh test world without other villagers, beds, bells, job-site blocks, villages, mods, or datapacks so that another point of interest cannot interfere with bed claiming.
Use Peaceful difficulty to prevent hostile mobs from attacking or distracting the villager during the nighttime test.
Keep particle rendering enabled at the highest available setting so that the green particles used by the report as the bed-claim confirmation are visible.

Do not break, move, replace, or add another bed after upgrading the world to Snapshot 3. Replacing the bed is explicitly described as restoring sleeping and would invalidate the intended trigger condition.

steps.action: Open the official Minecraft Launcher, select the Installations tab, enable visibility of snapshot versions if necessary, and create one installation for 26.1 Snapshot 2 and another for 26.1 Snapshot 3. Leave both on the same default game directory unless the world save will be copied manually between directories.
steps.exact_input: Installations -> enable Snapshots -> New Installation -> Version: 26.1 Snapshot 2; repeat with Version: 26.1 Snapshot 3
steps.success_cue: Two distinct Java Edition launcher installations are available: one labeled 26.1 Snapshot 2 and one labeled 26.1 Snapshot 3.

steps.action: Launch the 26.1 Snapshot 2 installation. Wait for the title screen to finish loading and verify that the displayed game version is 26.1 Snapshot 2.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft: Java Edition title screen identifies the running version as 26.1 Snapshot 2.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and begin creating a new world. Give it a recognizable name so that the same save can be selected after switching versions.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> Create New World -> World Name: MC-305691-pre-snapshot-3
steps.success_cue: The Create New World screen shows the world name MC-305691-pre-snapshot-3.

steps.action: Configure the world for deterministic setup: select Creative mode, enable commands if that is exposed as a separate option, set difficulty to Peaceful, select the Superflat world type, and disable structure generation. Do not enable experiments, bonus chests, datapacks, or custom world generation.
steps.exact_input: Game Mode: Creative; Allow Commands: On; Difficulty: Peaceful; World Type: Superflat; Generate Structures: Off
steps.success_cue: The creation screen is configured for a Creative, command-enabled, Peaceful Superflat world without generated structures.

steps.action: Create the world and wait until the terrain has fully rendered and player movement responds normally.
steps.success_cue: The player is standing on a flat Overworld surface in 26.1 Snapshot 2, nearby terrain is rendered, and movement is responsive.

steps.action: Ensure the green bed-claim particles will be visible. Open the pause menu, navigate to the video settings, set Particles to All or the highest equivalent setting, and return to the world.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Options -> Video Settings -> Particles: All -> Done
steps.success_cue: The world is active again with particle rendering set to All.

steps.action: Set the world to daytime so the source-world setup can be completed without immediately beginning the nighttime sleep attempt. Press T to open in-game chat, enter the command with its leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that the time was set, and the Overworld is visibly in daytime.

steps.action: Stand on an unobstructed area of the flat surface with several empty blocks around the player. Avoid building near any bed, villager, or village other than the ones created by this procedure.
steps.success_cue: A clear, level test area is available with enough room for one villager to walk to one bed.

steps.action: Summon one adult villager two blocks from the player. Press T to open chat, enter the command exactly with the leading slash, and press Enter.
steps.success_cue: Exactly one adult villager is visible approximately two blocks from the player in the clear test area.

steps.action: Obtain one bed from the Creative inventory. Press E to open the inventory, select the Search Items tab if necessary, search for bed, and place any one bed item into an empty hotbar slot. Close the inventory with E or Esc.
steps.exact_input: E -> Search Items -> search: bed -> move one bed to the hotbar -> E
steps.success_cue: One bed item is visible in the nine-slot hotbar at the bottom of the screen.

steps.action: Select the hotbar slot containing the bed by pressing its corresponding number key or scrolling the mouse wheel. Aim at the top of a flat ground block one to three blocks from the villager and right-click to place the bed. Leave open walking access along both sides and the foot of the bed, and leave at least two empty blocks of vertical space above it.
steps.exact_input: Select the bed's hotbar slot, then right-click the top surface of a nearby ground block
steps.success_cue: A complete bed is placed on the same ground level as the villager, within a few blocks of it, with no blocks obstructing access or headroom.

steps.action: Do not interact with the villager or bed. Remain close enough to keep the area loaded and wait for the villager to recognize and claim the bed. Watch the villager for the green particles specified by the report. Allow up to approximately 30 seconds of normal game simulation.
steps.success_cue: Green particles have been emitted by the villager, confirming the report's required bed-claim setup, while the original bed remains in place.

steps.action: Immediately preserve this claimed-bed state. Do not sleep in, break, move, or replace the bed. Press Esc and select Save and Quit to Title.
steps.exact_input: Esc -> Save and Quit to Title
steps.success_cue: The game has returned to the title screen after saving the world containing the villager and its claimed bed.

steps.action: Close the running game instance, return to the launcher, select the 26.1 Snapshot 3 installation, and launch it. Wait for the title screen and verify that the displayed version is exactly 26.1 Snapshot 3.
steps.success_cue: The Minecraft: Java Edition title screen identifies the running version as 26.1 Snapshot 3.

steps.action: Open Singleplayer and select the existing world named MC-305691-pre-snapshot-3. Do not create a replacement world. Start the selected world. If a snapshot or version-conversion warning is displayed, choose the option that creates a backup and then continues loading rather than canceling or opening without a backup.
steps.exact_input: Singleplayer -> MC-305691-pre-snapshot-3 -> Play Selected World -> create a backup and continue if prompted
steps.success_cue: The existing Snapshot 2 world begins loading in 26.1 Snapshot 3, with a backup created if the game offered that option.

steps.action: Wait until the converted world is fully loaded. Do not continue while terrain is missing, the loading overlay is visible, or movement and commands are unresponsive.
steps.success_cue: The player can move normally in the fully rendered Snapshot 3 world, and the test area is loaded.

steps.action: Locate the same villager and the same bed that were saved in Snapshot 2. Confirm that the villager is alive, the bed is still placed and unobstructed, and no additional bed has been added. Do not break or replace the existing bed even if the villager emits particles or wanders temporarily.
steps.success_cue: The pre-existing villager and its pre-existing, accessible bed are both loaded in Snapshot 3, and the bed has not been modified since the version change.

steps.action: Trigger the nighttime sleep attempt. While standing close enough to keep both the villager and bed loaded, press T to open in-game chat, enter the command exactly with its leading slash, and press Enter once. Do not place another bed or interact with the existing bed afterward.
steps.success_cue: Command feedback confirms that the time was set to night, the sky is dark, and the pre-existing villager and bed remain loaded and ready for immediate behavioral observation.

stor.handoff_condition: The original villager and the bed it claimed in 26.1 Snapshot 2 have been loaded unchanged in 26.1 Snapshot 3, and /time set night has just been executed. Begin observing the villager's nighttime interaction with that pre-existing bed without placing, breaking, moving, or replacing any bed.
uncertainties: The report clarification says only that the beds were placed before 26.1 Snapshot 3; it does not identify the exact source version. This plan uses 26.1 Snapshot 2 because it is the immediately preceding snapshot and therefore the smallest supported cross-version transition.

The report does not provide a world seed, coordinates, world type, game mode, difficulty, or exact villager-summoning command. The Superflat Creative setup, Peaceful difficulty, and /summon minecraft:villager ~2 ~ ~ command are practical deterministic choices rather than explicit report requirements.

The exact wording and button layout of the snapshot world-backup warning may vary. If a warning is shown, the required operation is to create a backup and continue opening the same world in Snapshot 3.

The initial description can be read as creating the villager and bed directly in Snapshot 3 and then reloading the area, but the reporter's later clarification identifies a pre-Snapshot-3 bed as the important missing condition. This plan prioritizes that clarification.

The report does not state how long after nightfall the observation was made. The handoff occurs immediately after setting night so that the separate observation subsystem can monitor the full sleep-attempt sequence.
